content.text: Your presentation layer is the editor

A headless CMS draws its editing UI from your data model, so a page becomes a stack of form fields that look nothing like the page. Uncial removes that fork. You write a Block once, as an ordinary Svelte component, and Uncial mounts it both in your site and inside the editor. The editor is the page, with editing chrome around it.
This page is a Content document managed by uncial-cms. This callout is a custom Block.

content.text: Scaffold a site
Inside an existing SvelteKit or Astro project, run:

pnpm add uncial uncial-cms
pnpm exec uncial-cms init
init
never overwrites a file. For SvelteKit it writes:

site.options.ts                       site options: content and static dirs
content/index.json                    the home page
src/lib/uncial/site.ts                the Site object: Blocks, Page templates, meta
src/lib/uncial/blocks/Note.svelte     a Block
src/lib/uncial/templates/Page.svelte  a Page template
src/routes/+layout.ts                 prerendering and trailing slashes
src/routes/[...path]/                 Content pages, and their Editor variants in edit/
src/routes/uncial/+page.svelte        the Dashboard
Astro gets the same site under
src/uncial/
and one
src/pages/[...path].astro
. Add the config lines
init
prints, run
pnpm dev
, and open
/edit/
Define a Block
A Block declares its id, label and attributes in its own
<script module>
BlockProps
types its props from them, and Field components make its text editable in place.
Stored documents name a Block by its
id
, so renaming the file orphans nothing.
Edit and render without the CMS
uncial
alone is an editor and renderer for any backend. Glob your Blocks into a Content model and hand it to both:

<script lang="ts">
	import 'uncial/styles';
	import { Renderer, createContentModel } from 'uncial';
	import { Editor } from 'uncial/editor';

	const model = createContentModel({
		blocks: import.meta.glob('./blocks/*.svelte', { eager: true })
	});
	let document = $state({ type: 'doc', content: [{ type: 'paragraph' }] });
</script>

<Editor {model} bind:json={document} />
<Renderer content={document} {model} />
